title: Jonah and the Safehouse
premise: Quentin Yarrow, a ghost in the private security world, takes a routine job protecting a whistleblower's courier—until a voiceprint he recorded years ago unlocks a server in Tallinn containing proof that a covert program he once served erased its own operatives, including the man whose identity Quentin has been living under. Hunted by the assassin who made those erasures and squeezed by three governments who each want the archive buried or owned, Quentin must decide whether the name he wears is a lie worth dying for. In the end he trades the archive for the assassin's employer, burns his borrowed identity, and walks out of the story as no one at all—free, finally, because there is nothing left to inherit.
about_author: August Delacroix is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade writing threat assessments for clients who preferred not to exist. Delacroix now writes thrillers from an undisclosed location, insisting only that the details are changed to protect the guilty.

chapters.title: The Courier Who Cried
chapters.summary: Quentin Yarrow takes a low-visibility job escorting a nervous courier through Marseille. POV: Quentin. The beat is quiet unease—the courier keeps checking mirrors, and so does Quentin, though neither will say what they expect to see.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: A dead-drop drive plays a recording of Quentin's own voice from 2011; when played aloud, it unlocks a remote server in Tallinn. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: vertigo—he never recorded anything like this, which means someone did it for him.

chapters.title: The Name on the Lease
chapters.summary: Quentin digs into his own identity documents and finds the paper trail predates his memory of acquiring them. POV: Quentin. Beat: creeping self-doubt—the first crack in the story he tells himself about who he is.

chapters.title: Tallinn, Briefly
chapters.summary: Quentin flies to Estonia and reaches the server farm minutes after someone else has died there for it. POV: Quentin. Beat: cold dread sharpening into resolve as he copies what he can and runs.

chapters.title: What the Archive Says
chapters.summary: Decrypted files reveal Program LANTERN: an operation that dissolved compromised agents by giving their identities to others—including Quentin's name, inherited from a terminated operative named Jonah Reyes. POV: Quentin with intercut files. Beat: grief for a stranger whose life he has been wearing.

chapters.title: The Man Who Erases
chapters.summary: Introduce Voss, the assassin tasked with reclaiming the archive, methodically closing on Quentin through hotel ledgers and flight manifests. POV: Voss. Beat: professional calm hiding something personal—Voss knew Jonah Reyes.

chapters.title: Three Flags
chapters.summary: A CIA liaison, an Estonian intelligence officer, and a French domestic agent each offer Quentin protection in exchange for the archive—and each lies about why. POV: rotating among the three. Beat: claustrophobia; every exit is an offer.

chapters.title: The Safehouse
chapters.summary: Quentin holes up in an old Program safehouse outside Gdańsk that the archive says was decommissioned—it wasn't. POV: Quentin. Beat: grim comfort; the building knows his habits better than he does.

chapters.title: Jonah's Letters
chapters.summary: Hidden in the safehouse wall: letters from Jonah Reyes to a daughter he was never allowed to meet. POV: Quentin reading. Beat: the inheritance theme turns intimate—Quentin realizes what was actually stolen.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: Voss finds the safehouse but doesn't shoot; instead she asks Quentin one question about Jonah that only someone who loved him would ask. POV: alternating Quentin/Voss. Beat: the enemy becomes ambiguous.

chapters.title: The Daughter
chapters.summary: Tracking the letters' addressee leads Quentin to Lena Reyes, a Lisbon archivist who has spent years asking why her father never existed in any record. POV: Lena. Beat: furious hope meeting cautious disbelief.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chips
chapters.summary: The three governments escalate: surveillance, a burned bank account, a staged arrest attempt. POV: Quentin. Beat: pressure tightening—the truth is now collateral in someone else's auction.

chapters.title: What Voss Was Told
chapters.summary: Voss reveals her contract includes killing whoever holds the archive—including her, eventually; she shows Quentin her own termination order. POV: Voss. Beat: bitter solidarity between two people the Program already spent.

chapters.title: The Auction
chapters.summary: Quentin offers fragments of the archive to all three governments simultaneously, buying time and sowing distrust among them. POV: Quentin. Beat: cold exhilaration—invisible man playing visible cards.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Archive Room
chapters.summary: Lena, desperate for her father's file, makes a side deal with the Estonian officer and nearly gets Quentin killed extracting her. POV: Lena. Beat: guilt and rupture—trust fractures along the fault line of grief.

chapters.title: Ghosts in the Protocol
chapters.summary: Deep in the archive, Quentin finds footage of his own recruitment: he wasn't recruited, he was installed, memory-wiped after Jonah's death. POV: Quentin. Beat: identity collapse—the man planning all this may be a fiction with his face.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Voss's employers, tired of waiting, send a second team; Voss breaks protocol to warn the safehouse, and the three of them survive a siege together. POV: alternating. Beat: forged loyalty under fire.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Quentin sets his real price: full public declassification of Program LANTERN and immunity for Lena and Voss—not money, not escape. POV: Quentin. Beat: justice outside the law, chosen deliberately.

chapters.title: Handover
chapters.summary: The exchange happens in a decommissioned lighthouse; the French agent tries to double-cross everyone, and Voss kills him to protect the deal. POV: Quentin. Beat: the cost made flesh—justice purchased with blood.

chapters.title: Debrief
chapters.summary: Governments honor the letter of the deal and gut its spirit; the archive goes public anyway via Lena's institution, unredactable. POV: Lena. Beat: imperfect vindication—the truth outlives the men who traded it.

chapters.title: The Last Erasure
chapters.summary: Quentin confronts the Program's surviving architect, learns the final truth about Jonah's death, and chooses not to kill him—instead erasing the architect's own records, giving him a taste of oblivion. POV: Quentin. Beat: climax resolved by restraint, not revenge.

chapters.title: No One at All
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Lena has Jonah's letters and a grave to visit; Voss has vanished on her own terms; Quentin burns his documents and walks into a crowd with no name, no file, no debt. POV: Quentin. Beat: quiet freedom—identity surrendered is identity finally owned.
